ranking.note: Raised to P2 and moved up: it is not generic backport churn — it corrects overstated privacy guarantees and mislabels an experimental feature in a shipping 31.2 release, which is the 'wrong documentation' case this category ranks first.
Raised to P2 and moved up to sit with #36319: both correct inaccurate privacy statements about -privatebroadcast that could mislead operators about their real network footprint.
Top of P3: missing/consolidated privacy documentation ranks just below correcting text that is actively wrong.

Moved down from its solo position: same band as the other P3s, but purely internal developer notes with no user-facing or release consequence, so it ranks below the user-facing notification, privacy and build-dependency docs.
Raised from P4 for consistency with #35395: both correct developer-facing documentation that is factually at odds with reality (58 of 129 LogError calls fatal) and causes recurring confusion.
Lowered to P4: unlike #36319 it carries no corrective content, only a BIP listing and release-note sync on a maintenance branch — narrow informational value.

inconsistencies: #36319 and #36401 are both fanquake maintenance-branch backports, but they are not equivalent: #36319 carries the private-broadcast experimental/risk-reduction correction and should be reviewed first; #36401 is BIP-461 listing plus release notes only.

#36348 and #35858 overlap on the same subject matter: #35858 moves i2p/tor privacy guidance into a new doc/privacy.md while #36348 edits doc/i2p.md in place. Their merge order matters (textual conflict and possible duplication); review #36348 first as the targeted factual correction, then fold its wording into #35858.

#35480 and #35518 are from the same author and both partially close issue #14278 (notification semantics). They are complementary, not duplicates — #35518 covers -*notify execution semantics generally, #35480 covers ZMQ reorg/eviction ordering — but reviewing them together avoids contradictory statements about ordering guarantees.

#36101 and #30361 both aim to end recurring contributor debates by writing down a convention; #36101 is project-wide and decision-forcing while #30361 is a narrow logging-guideline correction, so they correctly sit in different bands despite the shared framing.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly along the stated rule: text that is wrong or overstated about privacy (#36319, #36348) plus the one leverage-bearing design doc (#36101) at P2; missing documentation for things users and developers hit often at P3; a release-notes-only backport at P4. #36101 is kept at P2 rather than P1 because its concrete benefit is contested by maintainer NACKs, though the underlying decision it forces is real.
